resources.string: HTTPS tokens for the built-in git

The built-in git uses these when it clones, pulls or pushes HTTPS repositories on these hosts. Tokens are encrypted on this device, never included in backups, and never appear in commands, environment variables or the model context.
Saving a host that already exists replaces its user name and token. On GitHub use a fine-grained token with read and write access to Contents; GitLab and Gitea tokens work the same way.
Enter a host name such as github.com, optionally with a port (git.example.com:8443).
The user name must not be empty or contain spaces or colons.
The token must be printable ASCII without spaces.
Could not read the saved credentials.
Could not save the credentials. Try again.
Could not delete the credentials. Try again.
The built-in git will no longer authenticate to %1$s over HTTPS.
git@host:path and ssh:// remotes use an SSH host whose host key is pinned, for example host github.com with user git. The private key stays in the app.
